title: A New Ex Vivo Model for the Evaluation of Endoscopic Submucosal Injection Material Performance
protocol: Prepare specimens from the upper third of a porcine stomach.
Exclude specimens with submucosal elevation due to fibrosis.
Cut gastric specimens into squares approximately 6 × 6 cm in size.
Store cut gastric specimens at -30°C immediately after preparation.
Thaw frozen gastric specimens just before use for measurement procedures.
Stretch thawed specimens on a board using pins for the conventional ex vivo model.
Fix both ends of the specimen with clips to produce constant tension for the new ex vivo model.
Connect stainless-steel clip and key wire to S-shaped hook for setup.
Attach wire and S-shaped hook to weight for completion of setup.
Connect the hook to the other end of the wire.
Fix the pulleys at both ends of the base.
Place the rubber plate on the center of the base.
Place the gastric specimen on the rubber plate.
Pinch the specimen ends with the clip of the traction device.
Hang the weight through the pulley on each side.
Perform zero-point adjustment of the height gauge.
Push the PRESET button after fixing the scriber at the height of the mucosal surface.
Inject 2.0 mL of each solution horizontally into the submucosa from the specimen margins using a 2.5-mL syringe and 23-gauge needle.
Perform a submucosal elevation procedure.
Measure SEH promptly using a digital height gauge at 0, 2.5, 5, 7.5, 10, 12.5, 15, 17.5, 20, 30, 45, and 60 min after the injection.
Record the height displayed on the height gauge when fixing the scriber to the top of the submucosal elevation.
Perform three independent measurements.
Express the obtained results as the mean and standard deviation.
Analyze the obtained data using appropriate statistical software.
Evaluate the performance of SIMs.
